channel.title: Alabama Political Reporter - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Alabama Political Reporter (alreporter.com)

item.title: Legal Services Alabama announces 2026 Justice, Fairness, and Hope Awards recipients
item.description: A retired federal judge, the state bar president, and a long-serving state senator were honored for their advocacy supporting low-income Alabamians.

item.title: Mayor Steven Reed highlights Montgomery’s progress, major drop in crime
item.description: Reed cited major drops in violent crime and secured $50 million in federal grants during 2025, detailing progress in housing and downtown development.

item.title: Alabama lawmakers celebrate funding package’s passage, as DHS fight looms
item.description: The appropriations bills include more than $200 million in state earmarks, and gives Congress more time to negotiate DHS funding.

item.title: Senate advances bill limiting environmental rules beyond federal standards
item.description: Alabama Senate passed SB71, limiting state environmental rules to federal standards despite Democratic warnings about reduced protections for certain communities.

item.title: Public records show bankruptcies, foreclosure, tax lien as McKee runs for Congress
item.description: Records show the Republican candidate's adult life included nearly two dozen addresses across seven states and an evolving political identity before his recent Alabama residency.

item.title: Fairhope Library won’t move books after state aid loss
item.description: The library will soon be able to participate in the county courier service again after changes made Tuesday.

item.title: Republican gubernatorial candidate promises legal action against Tuberville
item.description: McFeeters is now promising to file a legal challenge to Tuberville’s entry on the ballot.

item.title: A new, unique gambling bill for the 2026 session
item.description: A gambling bill from Sen. Merika Coleman would allow people to vote on authorizing the Legislature and governor to pass gambling legislation.

item.title: Analysis | Alabama law—not property ownership—governs Tuberville eligibility
item.description: Property ownership does not determine residency under the Constitution, and long-settled Alabama case law makes that distinction clear.

item.title: Senate committee passes bill to OK digital driver’s licenses, nondriver IDs
item.description: An Alabama Senate committee quickly approved legislation requiring the state to offer digital driver’s licenses and IDs for a $15 fee.
